Volvo Car Plans Major Model Lineup Revamp
By Adria Calatayud
Volvo Car said it is making its largest-ever product push, launching 13 new car models by the end of the decade in an effort to revive its fortunes.

The Swedish carmaker--which is majority-owned by China's Zhejiang Geely Holding Group--said Thursday that it would roll out seven new car models for Western markets and six for China. The company said it aims to double its market share through a regionalized portfolio with electrified and all-electric cars, as well as third-generation hybrid models.
Volvo said it is targeting strong growth and cash flows over the long term, as well as an operating profit margin--a key profitability metric in the auto industry--above 8%.
Like many European auto peers, Volvo has been trying to bring down costs to stay competitive amid U.S. tariffs and pricing pressure due to the rise of the Chinese car industry.

The company said its new models for Western markets will use existing computing platforms and car architectures, which will allow investments in its technology stack and manufacturing to decline from current levels. In China, Volvo will work together with Geely on shared platforms and supply chains to boost efficiency, it added.
